top.line: Every article has a Pen, and my notes can be signed
top.para: On an iPad the system's menu hid the site's Highlight button, and feedback went through a chat. Every article now has a Pen: a bar at the foot while words are selected, private marks with comments, notes for the newsroom with their passages, and a browser key pki.sgit.ai vouches for that signs each note as mine.

in-short.line: Nine lines: the chat, the menu, the Pen, the key
in-short.para: Feedback went through a chat; the iPad menu covered the Highlight button. The Pen keeps marks private and sends notes when asked; a browser key vouched for in pki.sgit.ai's register signs them; of four ways to log in, the key per browser works now; the two vaults stay separate.

chat.line: Feedback on a page went through a chat window
chat.para: What I tell the newsroom about a page goes into a chat with its agent and loses where I was. The site had pieces, a Highlight button and the vault pane's notes with a lane, but in different places, and one did not work on the iPad I read on.

ipad.line: The iPad's menu sat where the Highlight button was
ipad.para: Safari's Copy, Look Up and Translate menu appears just above a selection, where the site put its Highlight button. Now the button goes below the selection on a touch screen, a bar at the foot offers Keep, Comment and Tell the newsroom, and the selection is kept as it is made.

pen.line: A Pen on every article, in four parts
pen.para: The Pen opens on the right beside the article: what is selected; my marks on this page with comments of my own, private and drawn on the page; notes for the newsroom with their passage, the vault pane's own records, sent down my lane; and who is signing.

key.line: A browser key that my pki.sgit.ai key operates
key.para: The register lets one key vouch for another both ways with an end date, built for agents. The Pen makes a key for this browser with pki.sgit.ai's code and hands over its submission; once my key operates it, every note is signed and anyone can check it from a pinned root.

login.line: Four ways to log in; the key per browser now
login.para: One passkey for both sites is a wider door than needed; a sign-in redirect is the end state but needs a page on pki.sgit.ai; a key per browser in the register works today; a QR code does its copying by camera. The browser key and the checks stay the same.

vaults.line: Two vaults, connected by keys, not a shared door
vaults.para: The reader vault and my pki.sgit.ai account stay separate so neither site's code can read the other's vault. The browser key connects them, next kept in the reader vault's master, and the reader vault's key can be sealed to my pki key. A login is a key, not a server account.

stands.line: Built, tested, and the first link is mine to make
stands.para: The Pen, the bar, the marks, the notes and the signing ship in this release, and the lane reader checks signed notes. I still have to send my browser's submission and link to it; the authorize page, the QR code, the key in the vault and the newsroom's own lane are next.

limits.line: No live signed note yet; the rest is proposed
limits.para: No note is checked against the live register yet; the browser's key is in browser storage; notes still need the vault's lane; the redirect and QR code are proposals; the iPad figure is drawn; the register's code is copied and refreshed with its hashes.

sources.line: A memo on an iPad, pki.sgit.ai, and the code
sources.para: My voice memo of 24 October, made on an iPad with a screenshot of its menu; pki.sgit.ai at v0.2.25, its guide, register and modules carried here unedited; the design note on signing in with a public key; the Pen's code, the lane reader and the test; card 090.
